family: Timed narration for video/slide synchronization — narration bound to beat-indexed visual timing rather than free duration (AUDIO-SCRIPT.md §16 'time-constrained narration'; editorial/VISUAL-STORY-COMPILATION.md; editorial/VIDEO-STORYBOARD.md).
primary_job: Carry the same verified argument as monologue or dialogue narration while meeting an externally imposed duration or beat-synchronization constraint, without unnatural time-stretching (AUDIO-SCRIPT.md §16).

thought_unit.unit: same listenably-complete-thought unit as audio/monologue (AUDIO-SCRIPT.md §4); this profile does not relax that rule to fit a clock.

rhythm.requirement: same natural-rhythm requirement as audio/monologue (AUDIO-SCRIPT.md §4). A duration budget is met by revising the script's scope, not by mechanically compressing sentence variety.

recurrence.policy: same recurrence discipline as audio/monologue (AUDIO-SCRIPT.md §6); a timed budget is not licence to cut a recurrence that restores orientation the visual timeline depends on.

scaffolding.rule: same restraint as audio/monologue (AUDIO-SCRIPT.md §7); do not add a spoken transition merely to bridge a visual cut — the transition still has to carry logic.

pace.default: rendering_mode is timed by default for this profile; target_duration_ms and tolerance_ms must be explicit before writing begins. A time budget is an editorial input, not permission to speed-warp the finished audio (AUDIO-SCRIPT.md §16).
pace.on_miss: when narration is materially too long or short for its budget, revise the spoken script within the verified claim set; do not stretch or compress the render until it sounds unnatural (AUDIO-SCRIPT.md §16, §21 'timing failure').

pronunciation_policy.requirement: same provider-neutral pronunciation glossary requirement as audio/monologue (AUDIO-SCRIPT.md §10, §11).

renderer_preference.rule: timed-narration is a synchronization layer over whichever narration mode the piece actually uses (monologue or dialogue), not a third voice mode of its own; renderer choice follows the underlying mode's own renderer_preference (AUDIO-SCRIPT.md §16, §23).

segment_identity.requirement: every segment carries a stable segment_id and a beat_id linking it to the shared argument-beat graph (editorial/VISUAL-STORY-COMPILATION.md §3 'canonical beat shape'), so a local narration or visual defect can be regenerated for one beat without recomputing the whole track (AUDIO-SCRIPT.md §17, §21).

beat_synchronization.requirement: narration and the visual/video timeline must agree on what is being asserted at each synchronized beat (editorial/VIDEO-STORYBOARD.md §2 'beat identity is the synchronization key'; editorial/VISUAL-STORY-COMPILATION.md §3).
beat_synchronization.boundary: timing alignment is a separate constraint from meaning; it does not authorize a new claim, and it does not force the narration to describe every visible on-screen action (AUDIO-SCRIPT.md §16; editorial/VIDEO-STORYBOARD.md §1).

audience_adaptation.general-reader: same monologue/dialogue audience adaptation as the underlying narration mode (editorial/profiles/artifact/audio-monologue.json, editorial/profiles/artifact/audio-dialogue.json audience_adaptation.general-reader), with pacing additionally bounded by the segment's target_duration_ms.
audience_adaptation.professional-generalist: same as the underlying narration mode's professional-generalist adaptation, bounded by segment timing.
audience_adaptation.domain-practitioner: same as the underlying narration mode's domain-practitioner adaptation, bounded by segment timing.
audience_adaptation.domain-expert: same as the underlying narration mode's domain-expert adaptation; a tight time budget for an expert audience should cut scope before it cuts density (editorial/profiles/audience/domain-expert.json anti_patterns: 'padding to reach an expected length').
audience_adaptation.beginner-learner: same as the underlying narration mode's beginner-learner adaptation; a tight time budget must not remove the higher useful_recurrence this audience needs (editorial/profiles/audience/beginner-learner.json modality_effects.audio) — cut scope instead.
audience_adaptation.child-upper-elementary: same as the underlying narration mode's child-upper-elementary adaptation (editorial/profiles/audience/child-upper-elementary.json modality_effects.audio); do not meet a duration budget by dropping the second, differently-worded restatement this audience needs.

acceptance: rendering_mode is explicit ('timed') with target_duration_ms and tolerance_ms recorded before compilation
every segment carries a beat_id resolving to the shared Visual Story Plan beat graph
a duration miss is resolved through script revision within the verified claim set, not through render-time stretching or compression (AUDIO-SCRIPT.md §16)
narration and the visual/video timeline agree on what is asserted at each synchronized beat
reject: a real duration constraint discovered only after writing and then solved by stretching or compressing the finished render
a segment with no beat_id when the destination requires beat synchronization
narration that describes every visible on-screen action instead of carrying the argument (AUDIO-SCRIPT.md §16)
free narration silently treated as timed, or the reverse, with no explicit rendering_mode recorded
status_note: Planning and canonical-script path only. TTS rendering and video/slide synchronization for this profile have not been exercised end to end; audio is deferred from the SUE-570 pilot and video remains 'reject for now' (docs/architecture/AUDIO-VIDEO-ROADMAP.md).
